Cada time ganha uma força de ataque e um: Each team gets an attacking and a defensive strength, calculated from the goals and the xG (expected goals) of all the season's matches: xG counts 75% and the score 25%. The calculation discounts the strength of the opponents the team faced, and recent matches weigh more: for every 90 days back, a match is worth half.
Com as forças dos dois times e a vantage: With the two teams' strengths and home advantage, a Poisson model (Dixon and Coles's, which gets the 0-0s and 1-1s right) gives the chance of each score in each remaining match.
O computador sorteia o resto da temporad: The computer plays out the rest of the season {n} times, match by match, and builds the final table of each run with the competition's criteria: points, wins, goal difference and goals scored. Each chance is the share of those seasons in which the team finished in the range: {exemplo}
O próximo jogo, a conta e para quem torc: The next match, the maths and who to root for.
Saem dos mesmos sorteios: o próximo jogo: They come from the same runs: the next match splits the seasons in which the team won, drew or lost; the maths gathers those that ended with each points total; and each match of the round is replayed with its three possible results, everything else equal, to see which one helps the team most.
O modelo só conhece gols e xG: não sabe: The model only knows goals and xG: it knows nothing of injuries, suspensions, manager changes or other competitions' fixtures. It's a chance, not a certainty, and the simulation is redone every round. See

O placar é o palpite do modelo, o mesmo: The score is the model's prediction, the same as in Simulate round by round: the favourite wins, except in the most balanced matches, which end in a draw, as many as the draws the model expects until the end; each result by its likeliest score. The likeliest exact score is often 1-1 even when there is a favourite, and it shows in the tooltip on hover. The bar shows the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win.
